I’m 73 this year, and I’ve farmed the same 8 mu outside our village for over fifty years. My son works in Shijiazhuang now, so it’s just me and my wife handling the fields. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on the fertilizer bags and understand what the extension technician says when he visits, but I don’t chase new fads — I stick with what has fed my family reliably. 

This year I’m keeping all 8 mu in the wheat-maize double crop. I don’t grow cotton anymore; at my age I can’t manage all that hand-picking and spraying. The winter wheat went in last October — improved shimai variety, same as my neighbor Lao Wang uses — and it’s greening up well. I rotary-tilled before sowing it. For the wheat I’ll irrigate four times: the winter irrigation is already done, and I’ll water again at jointing, heading, and grain-filling if the rain stays light. The extension man recommends about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, but I’d rather be a little safe than sorry, so I put down roughly 100 jin of compound fertilizer and topdress with urea, which comes to about 18 kg nitrogen, 10 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu. I’ll spray three times for weeds, rust, and aphids. 

For the summer maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in early June — there’s barely a week between crops, so I use no-tillage direct seeding. I buy hybrid seed, usually denghai 605, one package per mu. I fertilize with compound at sowing and topdress urea at the big-flare stage, about 15 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. Two irrigations are enough for maize if July brings any rain at all. I spray herbicide once and insecticide for corn borer once. I expect around 450 kg per mu of wheat and 500 kg per mu of maize if the weather holds. It’s not the highest yielding farm in the village, but it’s steady and I can manage it with my own two hands.
